'''Man Mohan Sondhi''' (18 December 1933 – 4 February 2018) was a prominent researcher in speech processing and signal processing who worked at [[Bell Laboratories]] during 1962–2001. He was famous for his research on [[echo cancellation]]. Born in [[Firozpur]], [[Punjab]], he was educated at [[Delhi University]], [[Indian Institute of Science]], and [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]].<ref>{{cite web |title=MAN MOHAN SONDHI |url=https://obits.nj.com/obituaries/starledger/obituary.aspx?n=man-mohan-sondhi&pid=188218114&fhid=11740 |publisher=The Star-Ledger |access-date=19 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The History of Echo Cancellation |url=http://www-labs.iro.umontreal.ca/~mignotte/IFT3205/Documents/Applications/EchoCancellation.pdf |publisher=IEEE Signal Processing Magazine |access-date=19 January 2021}}</ref>

As a specialist in speech science and [[signal processing]], Sondhi recognized that the future of satellite communications would require developing a technology to cancel the 600 millisecond signal echo created by the delay of transmission. Sondhi and his collaborators at Bell Labs eventually created the echo canceller that made practical satellite transmissions  possible.<ref>IEEE History Project http://www.ieeeghn.org/wiki/index.php/Man_Mohan_Sondhi</ref>
He received 5 patents.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.patentbuddy.com/Inventor/Sondhi-Man-Mohan/1391505|title=Man Mohan Sondhi, Inventor, Mountain Lakes, NJ}}</ref>

In 1998 he received the [[IEEE Eric E. Sumner award]].
